evidence.title: Bound the append-only anomaly log by shedding the append at a hard ceiling, not by shrinking the file
evidence.description: logs/anomalous.json had grown to ~115 MiB over 53 days with no rotation. In-place truncation or rename-rotation would blind the daemon/console tail readers on Windows (they track offsets or hold open handles), which the B2-LOGTH-041 throttle comment already warned about. The bound is therefore tail-safe: at or above AEGIS_ANOMALOUS_MAX_BYTES (default 64 MiB, 0 disables) the append is shed, counted as drops.log_size_cap (and DROPPED_COUNT), and the caller still receives SIZE_CAPPED so Case-2 findings keep delivering through the sensor pipe. The active file is never shrunk.

evidence.title: Forensic append cost is CRC32, not SHA-256; slicing-by-8 cuts it 4.1x bit-identically

Replaced std.hash.Crc32 (byte-at-a-time, ~537 MB/s) with a slicing-by-8 implementation of the identical ISO-HDLC function: 7.62 us -> 1.85 us, 4.1x, byte-identical output.

zig build test --summary all: 5/5 steps succeeded, exit 0 (forensic verifier and hash-chain tests unchanged)
evidence.finding: The pass assumed to be the hotspot (SHA-256) is 23% of the append; the cheapest pass (CRC32) carried 69% because Zig's std CRC is a byte-at-a-time table walk. Because slicing-by-8 computes the same function, the record format, hash chain, verifier and stored vectors are unchanged - the swap is provable by equality tests rather than by inspection. Rejected the SSE4.2 crc32 instruction: it is CRC-32C (Castagnoli) and would have changed every stored CRC. evidence.component: Windows host runtime (pipeline admission, FIM/ETW ingress mix)

evidence.finding: The measurement kills the capacity hypothesis the previous slice proposed. During churn the ingress demanded at least 157,000 events while the consumer drained ~1,000-1,250/s, and FIM alone shed 131,065 - one sensor's volume, not a marginal shortfall. Adding slots would need ~36x the queue (roughly 950 MB of static state) to absorb this burst, and 32,768 slots (+26 MB) would only have moved the boundary. The real lever is FIM ingress volume: aggregate or rate-shape repeated file-operation events at the sensor, or add per-source fair admission so an ETW/FIM storm cannot consume the whole host tail. Both change detection semantics or fairness policy, so they are recorded as the decision instead of being guessed into the code. Caveat: the burst was synthetic (a deliberately created 20,000-file churn), so its magnitude is a stress probe, not a host observation; the earlier organic burst was 10,408 drops.

evidence.title: Bounded diagnostic-log rotation closes unbounded growth that filled the system drive
evidence.description: The persisted diagnostic stream (RB013-LOG TeeSink -> <exe_dir>/../logs/aegis-daemon-diagnostic.log) had no size bound. evidence.title: Slice B1: both enforcement verbs refuse with DETECTION_ONLY before any gate, closing #25 at the control plane
evidence.description: Old flow: a privileged caller with a complete two-person ceremony could reach a block or quarantine handler that returned "status":"ENFORCED" with "host_effect_confirmed":true and a filter id. New flow: enforcementBlock and enforcementQuarantine return null with failure_code DETECTION_ONLY and failure_state REFUSED at the first statement, before the caller-role check, before payload parsing, before any PEP call or receipt. No authorization level, ceremony or payload can reach a host effect. The verbs stay registered so a legacy caller gets the product decision explained rather than an unknown-method error, and enforcement.unblock is untouched because it only cleans up filters that already existed. 232 lines of now-unreachable decision and receipt code were removed with the rewrite, so the claimed effect cannot be reconstructed from the handler.

evidence.limitations: E2: the refusal is proven in the Zig unit graph, not on a running service. The driver still contains the AegisWfpBlockFlow definition and the FWP_ACTION_BLOCK creation it performs; dispatch returns STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED so it is unreachable, and T11 pins that, but the code is not deleted because cl.exe/WDK is not on PATH here and an unbuilt driver edit would be an unverified change. evidence.title: The release bundler shipped an unsigned kernel driver over a signed one and omitted the minifilter; both are now gated and pinned
evidence.description: D1 exposed a packaging defect: package_release.ps1 copied build/x64/wfp/aegis_wfp.sys without checking its Authenticode status. The host was restored to the signed driver before the corrected bundle was installed.
evidence.limitations: E2: the gate and its test are static assertions over the packaging script; they do not sign a driver or load one. evidence.title: Minifilter FIM records ingress as kind packet_captured: no branch of pushDecodedFrame can produce fim_change
evidence.description: minifilter_reader.submitRecord builds its event with canonical.create(.minifilter), which sets event_type = .custom and leaves it there. event_queue.pushDecodedFrame maps .custom => .packet_captured, and its switch has no branch yielding .fim_change. Measured consequence in the heavy burst: 300,992 of 300,995 capture_fim events were counted and delivered as packet_captured with a file path in the payload, while the ETW lane tagged the same churn fim_change (358,570). Two sensors therefore disagree about the kind of the same activity, and any consumer keyed on fim_change cannot see minifilter records at all.

evidence.title: A daemon started before its kernel driver advertises DEGRADED forever: readiness is evaluated once and never re-checked
evidence.description: After the corrected install the deployed daemon reported state DEGRADED while all seven subsystems reported RUNNING. The state is decided once at startup and is not re-evaluated when the bridge appears. Restarting AegisNids with both drivers Running gave state RUNNING, 'Npcap capture loop starting', registry rule 2 matches on writes, and 18,838 events with 0 drops in 25 s across capture_wfp 6,762, capture_etw 6,814, capture_fim 5,251, capture_registry 9, capture_host_net 2. evidence.limitations: E5 on this host: proves the ordering effect and that the correct order yields RUNNING, not that every start order is safe. The 24 h soak has only just started and is IN_PROGRESS, not passed.

evidence.title: Acquisition-authored detection verdicts stripped at Zig ingress; the Go signature classifier is deleted, not just left dormant
evidence.component: src/pipeline/event_queue.zig (sanitizeAcquisitionClaim + ingress_authority counters), src/control/handler_registry.zig, nose/ (classifier deleted, AST guard added)
evidence.description: #28 required one detection authority. The v3 frame already carried evidence, but the wire's verdict fields were still believed: pushDecodedFrame copied producer rule_id/severity/event_type into IpcEvent, and detection_engine's ruleMatchDetector, blockEventDetector and severityDetector trusted them, so a producer asserting TypeMatch + rule id + severity produced a verdict with no Zig detection. sanitizeAcquisitionClaim now clears rule_id, zeroes severity and demotes .match_/.block/.ip_blocked to .forward at the single seam every wire producer passes, counting each removal in queue.stats.ingress_authority (claims_stripped + per-field breakdown). Red step first: the new ingress test failed with 'expected 0, found 12648430' (0x00C0FFEE) before the fix. Go side: nose/signature_classifier.go and its tests deleted, inject.go no longer claims Severity 1, and a new AST guard (nose/verdict_authority_test.go) fails if any non-codec file assigns EventType/RuleID/Severity or emits TypeMatch; the guard was proven to fire against an injected Severity: 2. No wire change: vectors, six codecs and struct_size are untouched.
commands: cd nose && go vet ./... && go test ./...
limitations: E2 only: no image was deployed for this patch, so no host observation of ingress_authority.claims_stripped exists yet.
The WFP driver header's rule_id/severity are now stripped; if the driver populates them, operator attribution for those rows must be re-homed into an evidence field in a separate slice.

The strip changes kind mapping for a producer-authored .match_ (now the evidence carrier, e.g. dns_query), which is intentional but is a behaviour change for any consumer that treated a wire .match_ as a detection.

evidence.title: S3-01 closed: the candidate-list test no longer writes tracked logs/; runtime paths have one redirectable resolver
evidence.description: AGENTS.md TEST HYGIENE item 2 forbids tests writing tracked tree state, and tests/security/test_candidate_labels.py created and unlinked logs/blocked_ips.json and logs/quarantine.json inside the repository, dirtying every later truth.py/release run depending on execution order. Four other runtime paths in tools/aegisctl.py (aegis_core.ndjson x2, canary_last.json, anomalous.json) still bypass the resolver; no current test writes them, so they are recorded as residual rather than fixed here.

The AEGIS_LOGS_DIR override is honoured by any process that sets it; the installed service does not, so production state cannot be moved by accident, but an operator shell could point the CLI elsewhere.

evidence.title: Every packaging entry point ships the same WDK driver image; the stale tree copy is unreachable
evidence.description: S2-05: installer/aegis.nsi packaged drivers\wfp_calloutegis_wfp.sys (28,136 B, Oct 16) while tools/installer.py, scripts/package_release.ps1 and tools/release_candidate.py shipped buildd\wfpegis_wfp.sys (42,896 B), so the deployed kernel image depended on which entry point an operator ran; the release candidate copies were additionally guarded by `if p.exists()`, letting it package a missing or stale image silently. evidence.title: Runtime stops claiming T1055 injection detection it never executes
evidence.description: S2-03. Three places claimed a live injection detector and none was live: src/daemon.zig constructed an InjectionDetector and destroyed it without ever calling ingest(); src/contract/runtime_manifest.zig hard-coded c.has_injection_detector = true (unlike the probed flags beside it), so every feature negotiation was answered wrongly; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md described a 'REAL-time ETW path' that does not exist. The daemon has no InjectionEvent producer at all: the ETW session parses process/file/registry providers into IpcEvents and carries no process-open, thread-create, VirtualAllocEx or image-load opcodes. The construction, its import and the flag are removed/falsified with the reason in place, the doc rows are corrected to NOT WIRED, and tests/security/test_capability_claims.py pins the rule in both directions: the flag may not be re-asserted (mutation control: restoring = true fails it), a returning InjectionDetector.init must be accompanied by an .ingest call site, src/daemon.zig may not carry imports it never uses, and the NOT WIRED documentation may not silently revert. zig build and zig build test both pass; full python suite 1092 passed / 4 skipped.
limitations: E2 only: nothing was observed on a host; T1055 detection remains unimplemented in production.
Wiring the detector needs new ETW opcode parsing and an InjectionEvent producer, plus a detection-identity path into the pipeline - a separate slice with an E5 gate.

Two injection implementations still overlap in source (ProcessInjectionDetector in windows/host_telemetry_detectors.zig and detection/injection_detector.zig); choosing one is an owner design decision.
Six other runtime_manifest flags are still hard-coded true (has_federation, has_tls, has_xdr, has_replay, has_forensic_pipeline, has_fault_injection) and this pin does not cover them.

evidence.title: A closed readiness gate now names the condition that closed it
evidence.description: S1-05 residual. `aegisctl readiness` could answer ready:false / overall_gate:false with failure_reasons: [] and degraded_components: [] - a release gate that refuses without an actionable cause. cmd_readiness is now build_readiness(payload), a pure function whose reason list is built from the same conditions the gate tests: state, the six worker flags, rules, degraded subsystems, plus degraded_without_named_component when the aggregate degraded flag cannot be attributed, and a construction guard gate_closed_without_named_cause. Gate semantics are unchanged; only the refusal's explanation. 19 focused tests pass, including a mutation that disables the degraded branch; the live payload on this host now reports [degraded_without_named_component, state_degraded] instead of an empty list. E2 plus E1 live reading, not E5: no daemon behaviour changed.
limitations: E2 plus E1 only: the decision function is tested and the CLI was read on the installed daemon; no host behaviour changed.
The aggregate `degraded` flag is still not itemised inside the daemon (state_machine.zig / control_api.py); the CLI now names the gap instead of hiding it.

The gate remains worker-flag based; whether a stopped non-required subsystem (e.g. rust_pep in detection-only mode) should close the gate is an owner product decision.

evidence.title: ETW storm shed now protects the signal classes inside the source share
evidence.description: The live 8.93 h soak on source c79c5a1 lost 148,217 rows, all capture_etw (145,915 fim_change + 2,302 reg_change), with shed_overload=0 and source_quota_shed=148,217. Root cause: the deliberate storm policy shed Write/NameDelete only at the global 3/4 queue line (12,288), while admission refuses a host source at SOURCE_OCCUPANCY_CAP (7,168), so a file-write burst filled the ETW share first and the registry/process rows were refused by the same quota. The callback now uses etwSharePressure(depth, occupancy): shed low-value classes when EITHER the queue is 3/4 full OR this source is within ETW_SHARE_MARGIN=256 of its own cap, leaving a bounded reserve for ProcessStart/CreateKey/SetValueKey. The first-sighting exemption and its 200-token bucket are unchanged. Pacing the ETW callback was rejected because the helper exposes no EventsLost counter, so a pause would convert counted queue loss into uncounted kernel loss. zig build test: 2,085 passed / 10 skipped / 0 failed; zig build exit 0. E2 only: the finding was measured on the previous build and this policy has not been deployed or re-measured.
limitations: E2 only. The 148,217-drop measurement was taken on the previous build; this patch must be deployed and the soak re-run before any E5 claim.
It does not make the soak zero-loss: write storms still lose rows, now as shed_overload (policy, first sighting exempt) rather than source_quota_shed (overflow).
The 256-slot reserve is not a guarantee: the exemption bucket can release up to 200 writes in a burst, and a registry storm can still exhaust the share.
shed_overload is exposed on queue.stats but not in the health payload the soak tool reads, so a soak can pass while policy shed is nonzero. That honesty gap is recorded, not fixed.
Extending storm shed to the per-source boundary changes which rows are lost first; the acceptable loss budget is an owner decision.

evidence.title: The soak verdict counts deliberate policy shed, not just health loss
evidence.description: QLOSS-ETW-PRIORITY-001 moves low-value ETW file writes/deletes from source_quota_shed (inside data_integrity.queue_dropped_total) to shed_overload, which is exposed only on queue.stats. host_soak_check.py read only health, so the same discarded rows could leave the counter the soak reads and a zero-loss 24 h window could pass while the queue was still shedding. The tool now reads queue.stats, takes --shed-budget (default 0), fails when shed_overload exceeds it, and fails closed when queue.stats is unavailable; the report carries shed_overload and shed_budget. 11 focused tests pass; the live 8.9 h run still fails on its real 148,217 drops with shed_overload=0.
limitations: E2 plus E1: the verdict logic is tested and read live; no host behaviour changed.
The default budget of 0 keeps R-08 strict; an owner-approved shed rate must be passed explicitly and then appears in the report.
queue.stats availability is now a soak precondition; an older daemon without the command fails the gate instead of being skipped.

evidence.title: 448 minifilter rows overflow the 4 MiB boot ring before the daemon attaches
evidence.description: First soak after the 2026-11-11 01:30 reboot failed at 0.06 h with minifilter_ring_dropped=448, queue_dropped_total=0, shed_overload=0. queue.stats: reads=5700 rows=92562 ring_written=113754 dropped=448 pipeline_dropped=0. The 4 MiB ring holds roughly 113k 36-byte records; the daemon process started about 2m25s after boot and the minifilter was already emitting into the ring with no reader attached, so 448 of 113,754 boot records did not fit (0.39%). The driver DroppedEvents is a gauge that survives a daemon restart; only a driver reload zeroes it, which is why a soak armed from the boot state cannot pass at loss-budget 0. This is a kernel-ring loss, distinct from the ETW admission loss measured in QLOSS-ETW-PRIORITY-001. Options recorded: 8 MiB ring (driver candidate), earlier reader attach (source), or a disclosed startup limitation. The 01:29 deploy attempt never replaced the binary (installed image still ED74E56F), so these numbers are from the old build; the new build has not been measured. The loader (boot-sequence.ps1) carried the same array-$Matches defect: its State returned UNKNOWN for a RUNNING service, exhausting both drivers' retry budgets and inflating the gap; it now joins sc.exe output to one string. The 01:42 elevated deploy attempt also failed on the same defect (State UNKNOWN -> stop skipped -> Copy-Item hit the mapped image); the deploy script now joins output, captures the PID before stop, waits for exit, retries the copy, and restores the service on abort.
limitations: E1: host reads only; no fix has been applied.
Measured on the old deployed build (ED74E56F, source c79c5a1). The 4c4ed3a build was not deployed by the 01:29 window.
The exact deploy termination is not recorded; the script's new elevation guard and trap close that gap for the next run.
A driver reload resets the gauge for the steady-state window; it does not fix the boot blind spot.

The host boot model is not what the installer ships: tools/installer.py:263 creates AegisNids with start=auto and never registers AegisBootSequence, so a fresh install would reintroduce the AUTO_START-before-drivers gap. Packaging slice still open.

evidence.title: Minifilter reader retries the port every second so the boot ring can start empty
evidence.description: After the 2026-11-11 demand-start change, the 01:49 boot still lost 4,012 minifilter rows (ring_written=188,653, reads=7,322, rows=190,191, pipeline_dropped=0) because the boot task started the minifilter before the daemon and the 4 MiB ring (~116k 36-byte records) could not hold the >16k records/s boot burst for the ~7 s daemon init. Starting the daemon first is the only order that starts the ring empty: the minifilter reader is a retry loop, so it can already be waiting when the driver loads. The retry interval was 10,000 ms, which could let the reader sleep through the driver's first seconds and rebuild the backlog; it is now 1,000 ms. The host boot script is reordered (WFP -> daemon -> minifilter) and its sc.exe State parser is fixed. zig build test: 2,085 passed / 10 skipped / 0 failed; zig build produces 21A875CF8F103E3B. E2 only: the new build has not been deployed or rebooted yet.
limitations: E2 only. The 4,012-row measurement was taken on 4c4ed3a; 21A875CF has not run on the host.
The boot order fix lives in admin-evidence/host-window-003 (local-only); the installer still ships no boot task and creates AegisNids AUTO_START.
A 1 s port retry is more probes while the driver is absent; it does not change the 50 ms steady-state pull loop.
If the boot storm outruns the reader for more than ~7 s after the driver loads, the 4 MiB ring can still overflow; that would need a driver-side ring increase.

evidence.title: Daemon-first boot with a 1 s minifilter retry: zero ring loss on the host
evidence.description: Installed 21A875CF8F103E3B (source 1ca18c4) on the Windows host and rebooted at 2026-11-11 02:09:14. The fixed boot task started AegisNids at 02:09:50 and AegisMinifilter at 02:09:53 (daemon first), so the reader was already retrying (1 s cadence) when the ring was created. Result: services all RUNNING, health state RUNNING with degraded=false, minifilter_ring_dropped=0, queue_dropped_total=0, no SCM 7031/7034 since boot. The same boot produced shed_overload=18,035 from the ETW admission policy during the boot write storm; its delta over the next 120 s was 0 with 31,868 more rows pushed, so it is a boot transient, not a steady shed. This closes the boot-ring loss measured at 448 (01:30, AUTO_START/driver-first/10 s) and 4,012 (01:49, DEMAND_START/driver-first/10 s) on this host and build.
limitations: One lab host, one boot; not fleet behaviour.
The 24 h soak (R-08) is still open; this record covers the boot path only.
The boot order and task are local-only; the installer still ships AUTO_START and no loader.
The 18,035 ETW policy shed at boot is accepted as a transient here and excluded from the steady-state window by a deliberate daemon restart; it is not zero-loss evidence for the ETW lane.

evidence.title: 30.8 h on 21A875CF: no crash, no ring loss, ETW admission still bounded-loss
evidence.description: 30.81 h window (2026-11-11 05:56:58 -> 2026-11-12 12:44:49) on installed 21A875CF8F103E3B (source 1ca18c4), daemon pid 8160. evidence.title: ETW file writes outside the rule-actionable paths are filtered at the source
evidence.description: The 30.8 h window showed 8,850,070 ETW file writes holding the ETW share while 1,394 registry rows were quota-dropped and 446,327 rows were policy-shed. Rule audit: R1001/R1004 match System32 paths, R1005 matches System32\drivers\etc\hosts, R1003 matches Startup, R1002 is a create/rename signal delivered by the minifilter; no rule matches an arbitrary write. New shouldAdmitEtwWrite(path) admits empty paths, isCriticalPath paths (System32/SysWOW64/drivers\etc), any path containing \windows\system32\ or \windows\syswow64\ (ETW may use an NT device path), and \Startup\ paths, and filters the rest at the ETW callback before they consume the share. Filtered rows are counted in file_write_filtered, published on queue.stats.etw and the CLI; NameDelete, registry and process rows are unchanged. zig build test: 2,087 passed / 10 skipped / 0 failed; zig build produces 25AB91543EBC90F5. E2 only: the expected collapse of shed and registry overflow must be measured in the next window. A write that passes the predicate is also exempt from the storm shed, so a System32 write is never the policy-discarded row. The live 16 min check showed file_write_filtered=0 with 186k writes because the Write event's FileName did not reach file_path; a write with no decoded path is now filtered unless the raw TLV FileName (kind 3 only, not ImageName) contains a protected tree.
limitations: E2 only; 25AB9154 has not been deployed or measured.
It is a coverage decision: generic file writes are no longer evidence. R1002/R1004 still see file creation via the minifilter, but future rules that need arbitrary writes must revisit this filter.
Anomaly-detector baselines shift because fim_change volume falls; thresholds were not retuned.
NameDelete (606,234 in 30.8 h) is still admitted; if it becomes the pressure point it needs its own rule audit.

evidence.title: 25.3 h with the write filter: loss down 98.6 %, registry overflow remains
evidence.description: 25.33 h window (2026-11-12 14:11:57 -> 2026-11-13 15:31:41) on installed 33223B2CC59DE177 (source a9dd914), daemon pid 24396. Total loss 6,257 of 23,850,132 pushed = 0.0262 %, down 98.6 % from the 30.8 h window (447,722). Per-24 h rates: ~2,747 queue drops (0.0269 % of registry) and ~3,180 shed (0.71 % of the 472,991 admitted deletes). Verdict at 0/0 is FAIL; the remaining loss is ETW admission only, with the queue peak (7,176) at the ETW share cap (7,168).

One lab host, 25.3 h; not fleet behaviour.

evidence.description: Owner accepted the measured ETW loss envelope on 2026-11-13 (option A). evidence.title: Health and readiness honour the owner-approved loss budget
evidence.description: RC-CLOSEOUT accepted a 3,500 queue / 4,000 shed envelope, but state_machine.zig used counter != 0 for data_loss_observed, so the 25.33 h window (2,900/3,357) reported DEGRADED and readiness false; host_soak_check --loss-budget could not pass because it checks health independently. evidence.title: User-hive registry watcher, named registry alerts, and the key path in the record
evidence.description: The HKCU Run canary produced no alert. Three defects: startAll opened only two HKLM roots, so HKCU rule 3 had no watcher; a SYSTEM service's HKCU is SYSTEM's hive, not the interactive user's; and registryThread pushed an empty payload, so any registry alert was unattributable (payload_len=0). startAll now enumerates HKEY_USERS and opens <SID>\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run for every loaded hive; each watcher carries an event path (HKU\<SID>\...\Run, SID retained) and a match path (HKCU\...\Run, one rule for all users); rule 3 is registered; the key path is pushed as the event payload; and CLI enrichment maps native ids 1/2/3 to REG-HKLM-RUN / REG-HKLM-SERVICES / REG-HKCU-RUN instead of UNKNOWN_RULE. zig build test: 2,091 passed / 10 skipped / 0 failed; zig build produces 680510ABB14E328A. E2 only: the host has not run the new build or the HKCU canary.
limitations: E2 only; the host has not run 680510AB or the HKCU canary.
Hives loaded after the registry thread starts are not watched until restart; logon-time monitoring needs a re-scan.
The watcher fires on any change under the Run key (RegNotify does not report the value name).
ETW registry paths are still not normalized into the HKCU rule; the native watcher is the authority.
Forensic retention (~16k records) still requires prompt querying.

evidence.title: HKCU Run canary detected on 680510AB with the SID-bearing key path
evidence.description: Installed 680510ABB14E328A (source e4c2188). Created HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run value AegisCanaryE5, waited 1 s, and scanned alerts. Result: REG-HKCU-RUN, severity High, source registry_sensor, verified=true, payload_len=94, record_seq=114434. The daemon log named the hive: 'registry change matched rule 3: HKU\S-1-5-21-2240144573-294256931-834073773-1001\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run'. The chain is user hive -> HKU<SID> watcher -> rule 3 (match HKCU path) -> forensic record carrying the HKU path -> named alert. The canary value was removed after capture. ALERT-SCAN-001: forensics.list pages oldest-first and alerts capped at 5 pages/want, so the first attempts returned only R1004 noise; alerts now anchors the scan 4,096 records before the ring tip and the E5 capture used --limit 1000.
limitations: One host, one loaded user hive, one canary.
Hives loaded after the registry thread starts are not watched until restart.
RegNotify reports the watched root, not the value name.
Forensic retention is ~16k records; prompt querying or the anchored scan is required.
A --rule filter for alerts is not implemented; R1004 noise can still fill the early page.

evidence.title: hosts path rule detected on the host, and it fires on a read
evidence.description: Installed 680510ABB14E328A (source e4c2188). A read-only Get-Content of C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts, followed by the anchored alert scan (--limit 5000), returned five R1005 'hosts File Modification' alerts (seq 231465-231469 and 232488, payload 58/99 bytes, source file_sensor, verified=true) and two R1001 'System32 Write Attempt' alerts (payload 42), plus 677 R1004 DLL noise records. The read did not modify hosts. This closes the earlier 'R1005 = 0' ambiguity (the alert scan was reading the oldest ring pages), and exposes a detection-quality defect: the minifilter lane emits IRP_MJ_CREATE for read-only opens, and the path rules have no operation filter, so reading hosts raises a High 'modification' alert and reading System32 raises 'write attempt'. Detection-only was confirmed simultaneously: enforce status shows prevention_gate=closed, host_effect_capable=false, host_effect_confirmed=false; the alert's action=Block is catalog intent, not a host effect.
limitations: One host, one read canary.
The path rules fire on open/read, not only write; operation-level filtering is not implemented.
The alert action 'Block' is catalog intent; detection-only was confirmed by enforce status.
R1004 noise (677 in the same window) still crowds the alert surface; a --rule filter is the next ergonomic fix.
Forensic retention still requires the anchored scan and a large limit.

evidence.title: Minifilter emits only write/create intent, not every read-only open
evidence.description: R1005 and R1001 fired on a read-only Get-Content because AegisPostOperation emitted every successful IRP_MJ_CREATE. The record struct has no desired-access field, so the classification is done in the driver without an ABI change: AegisPreCreate NULL-guards the create security context, then reads DesiredAccess (FILE_WRITE_DATA/APPEND/WRITE_ATTRIBUTES/DELETE/WRITE_DAC/WRITE_OWNER) and the CreateDisposition high byte (SUPERSEDE/CREATE/OVERWRITE/OVERWRITE_IF), stores a one-bit sentinel in the callback context, and AegisPostOperation returns immediately when ctx is NULL. No record/IOCTL/ring/user-ABI change; the post-op does not touch the possibly-freed security context. WDK build: 10,240 bytes, unsigned 9C627F0F; test-signed Valid 8AC348372321ECFE5BD535B9A9A19F6F6567C58145395359764AFCAF5C2480E0. Two source pins pass. E2 only: the host has not deployed the driver or run the read/write canary.
limitations: E2 only; the driver has not been deployed or measured on the host.
FILE_OPEN_IF with read-only access is treated as read-only even if it creates.
Rename/delete via SetInformation is still not emitted.
Test-signed driver; no production signing custody.
FIM volume reduction has not been measured over 24 h.

evidence.title: Read-only opens no longer alert; hosts writes and DLL drops still do
evidence.description: Deployed the write-intent minifilter (pre 10C41E80, post 8AC348372321ECFE, service RUNNING, health RUNNING, ring 0) and ran four canaries. Read hosts: R1005=0. Write hosts: R1005=2 (seq 6610/6611). Restore hosts (a write): R1005 at 7413/7414/7493. Read kernel32.dll: R1004=0. Drop benign .dll in System32: R1004=1 (seq 8034) + R1001 8035/8064. The read-only captures contain no new R1005/R1004; the write captures do. Background R1001 records in the read capture (16, seq 2354-3825) are legitimate System32 writes by services, not the hosts read: R1001 matches every System32 path and the host writes there continuously. The operation filter fixed the read-trigger class; R1001's breadth is a separate rule-tuning issue. All canary artifacts cleaned: hosts restored, DLL removed, HKCU key removed.
limitations: One host, one driver swap, one canary set.
Test-signed driver; no production signing custody.
R1001 is broad and fires on legitimate System32 writes; not addressed here.
FILE_OPEN_IF read-only is treated as read-only even if it creates; rename/delete via SetInformation is not emitted.
FIM volume reduction was not measured over 24 h.

evidence.title: The 24 h soak gate scored cumulative counters, so a deploy burst spent the whole budget before the window began
evidence.description: After the write-intent minifilter deploy at 17:11 on 2026-11-14, the fresh daemon showed queue_dropped_total 0 but shed_overload 5,310 in ~2 h, above the owner's 4,000/24 h envelope, so the soak gate failed. Two queue.stats samples 60 s apart showed shed_overload flat at 5,310 while 16,347 rows were pushed: the loss was a burst in the first minutes after restart (minifilter ring draining plus the FIM/HKCU canaries at 17:11-17:12), not sustained loss. The gate was comparing cumulative process counters against a per-window budget, so the deploy's own burst consumed the 24 h allowance and no later window on that process could pass. Fix: --baseline auto|<path> snapshots data_integrity + shed_overload at window start and gates growth since the anchor, failing closed on growth over budget, on a counter that went backwards (restart), and on a counter missing from the payload or the baseline; every report carries counters_absolute and counters_delta so the pre-window burst stays visible. Without --baseline the historical absolute comparison is unchanged, so the existing PASS artifacts reproduce exactly. Also hardened: a missing loss counter is now a problem instead of being skipped. 15 tests in test_soak_verdict.py (6 new), 439 in tests/security+tests/tools+tests/docs; a live --baseline auto run reported IN_PROGRESS with all deltas zero and the 5,310 pre-window sheds reported absolutely.
limitations: The 24 h window this patch starts has not finished; the entry records the gate fix, not a completed soak.
Absolute budget semantics are unchanged when --baseline is omitted, so an operator who does not pass a baseline still gets the old (stricter, window-poisoning) behaviour.
The baseline is a snapshot, not a series: a restart between anchor and check voids the window rather than resuming it.

evidence.title: One tracked command now answers the clean-host boot gate, and it refuses to pass a hand-fixed host
evidence.description: INSTALLER-BOOT-MODEL-001 shipped demand-start services, the AegisBootSequence task and AEGIS_LOSS_BUDGET, but its E5 gate was six checks a human had to remember after a fresh install and reboot — the same shape of oversight that produced the 2026-11-11 boot failure. tools/host_preflight.py reads sc qc, the service Environment registry value, schtasks /v, the driver states and the control pipe, and emits a JSON verdict over 12 checks: service start type is DEMAND_START, the loss budget is on the service, the boot task exists/enabled/SYSTEM/last-result 0, the task's loader lives under the install directory, both drivers are RUNNING, the daemon is RUNNING and not degraded with the same budget, minifilter_ring_dropped is 0, and the daemon has an optional uptime floor. Every check fails closed on an unreadable value. Live run on the lab host: 11 PASS + 1 FAIL naming boot_task_loader_installed, because that host is hand-fixed from admin-evidence and never ran the installer — exactly the distinction a boot gate must not blur. 10 pins in tests/release/test_host_preflight.py cover each failure mode (AUTO_START, lab loader, failed task, missing task, stopped driver, unreadable health, ring loss, budget mismatch, uptime floor) plus a check-set census so the rules cannot shrink silently. Full suite: zig build test EXIT 0, pytest 1,118 passed / 7 skipped.
limitations: E2 + a live run on a hand-fixed lab host. A clean-host install + reboot + preflight run is still the E5 gate and has not happened.
The tool cannot tell a fresh install from an install over an old one; the upgrade path remains untested.
It does not verify installed binary digests — stage_helpers.py --check owns those, and duplicating them here would create a second source of truth for the same hashes.

evidence.title: Every runtime path in aegisctl now goes through the one redirectable resolver
evidence.description: TEST-HYGIENE-S301 closed the two candidate-list commands and recorded five remaining hand-built runtime paths as residual: aegis_core.ndjson in _event_log_candidates and in the _event_log_path fallback, canary_last.json on read and write, and anomalous.json for the brain inbox. Same defect class: a path no fixture can redirect, so a test or lab run that exercises the command writes tracked tree state or reads the wrong file. All five now go through _logs_dir() (AEGIS_LOGS_DIR override, production default <repo>/logs). Pinned structurally: the literal TOOLS_DIR.parent / 'logs' may appear exactly once, inside the resolver, and the other spellings are refused; plus behavioural proof that canary report reads a receipt from AEGIS_LOGS_DIR (exit 0) and that with no receipt it reports available=false, exit 3, creating no file. 4 tests in the new file, 428 across tests/security+tests/tools.
limitations: E2 only: no host execution belongs to this patch.
Other tools/*.py files were not audited for the same pattern; the claim is scoped to tools/aegisctl.py.

evidence.title: The clean-host gate is now two commands, and the runbook cannot report a verdict it did not reach
evidence.description: RC-FINAL item 5, INSTALLER-BOOT-MODEL-001 and PREFLIGHT-001 all ended at the same unrun procedure: install on a clean host, reboot, verify the boot model. A remembered checklist is how the 2026-11-11 boot failure survived review, so scripts/e5-clean-host.ps1 reduces it to -Stage Install (elevated: hash-assert the installer, silent install, reboot) and -Stage Verify (post-reboot: host_preflight.py with a 5 min uptime floor + a 24 h soak window anchored with --baseline auto), writing both JSON artifacts into admin-evidence/e5-clean-host-<ts>/. The runbook fails closed on non-elevation, on a missing installer, and on a hash mismatch; -DryRun prints every command and changes nothing; a dry run prints 'SKIPPED (dry run)' and 'RESULT: DRY-RUN' rather than PASS, because Invoke-External returns 0 without running; and the soak anchor is taken even when preflight fails. Exercised on the lab host: install dry run detected the freshly built dist/aegis-installer-5.0.0.exe (sha256 B618AE7B..., 6,129,989 bytes) and printed the plan; Verify without elevation was refused; Verify dry run printed the plan and claimed nothing; a missing installer failed non-zero. The installer was rebuilt from current source, re-proving the boot-model packaging is buildable. 14 pins across the runbook and the preflight gate. This is E2 by design: no clean host has run it.
limitations: E2: the clean-host install and reboot have not happened, so the boot-model E5 gate stays open.
The install stage's silent NSIS switch (/S) is exercised only as a printed plan here; the real install path was last proven by the hand-run window on 2026-11-14, not by this script.
The runbook cannot restore a clean image; using it on a dirty host produces evidence about that host, not about a fresh install.

evidence.title: The audit tool no longer calls a complete component audit a shippable release
evidence.description: tools/final_audit.py printed '100% PRODUCTION VERIFIED' whenever the component audit (66/66 modules across ten dimensions, five specialized holds, golden path declared) was complete, while RC-FINAL-20261114 recorded ~85% for a shippable release: a contradictory-source-of-truth pair, which AGENTS.md makes a stop-the-line condition. The declaration is now split: component_audit COMPLETE/INCOMPLETE, and release SHIPPABLE/NOT SHIPPABLE computed from six fail-closed gates — truth.py verify, the component audit, a release signature (signature + public_key + signed_digest whose digest matches the SHA256SUMS it covers), a clean-host preflight PASS whose boot-task loader lives under the install directory (so a hand-fixed lab host cannot close it), a 24 h soak with required_hours >= 24, verdict PASS, no problems and a checked_at after the newest runtime-tree commit (an older PASS is reported as predating the build, and unreadable freshness fails closed), and the evidence-debt ratchet. The live board reports component audit COMPLETE, release NOT SHIPPABLE with three open gates naming their owners (signature=owner, clean_host=owner, soak=time); --check keeps the component meaning, --release-check exits 1 while any gate is open. 16 pins in tests/release/test_release_board.py cover each way a false ship verdict could be produced, including an AST pin (docstring removed) that refuses the string '100% PRODUCTION VERIFIED' in executable code. docs/gates/T20_100pct_audit.* keep their names but now carry both halves; CONTRIBUTING documents the two checks.
limitations: E2: the gate logic is pinned, but the gates themselves are open on this host — the board shows what is unproven, it does not prove it.
Release gates are evaluated against local artifacts under admin-evidence/, which is git-ignored; on a different machine the board reports the gates open until that machine records its own evidence.
Soak freshness is compared with the commit time of tracked runtime paths; an uncommitted runtime change is invisible to that rule (the soak would look fresh for a build that is not the working tree).
The signature gate proves a signature artifact covers the exact SHA256SUMS bytes; it does not verify the cryptography (that needs the custodian's public key, which is the point of the owner gate).

evidence.title: The bundled installer never created its services on a clean host: sc.exe writes to stdout
evidence.description: scripts/install_aegis.ps1 guarded both service registrations with the OUTPUT of `sc.exe query` (`$driverSvc = sc.exe query AegisWfp`; `if (-not (sc.exe query AegisNids))`). Measured on the host: querying an absent service exits 1060 and writes 122 characters to STDOUT, so the output is always truthy, `-not` is always false, and neither `sc.exe create` ran on a machine without the service — the exact clean-host case the guard existed for. The bundle install would copy files, skip both creates, install the boot task, warn on `sc.exe start`, and print 'Installed AEGIS NIDS' on a host with no AegisNids service and no AegisWfp driver. The NSIS installer was unaffected because tools/installer.py issues sc create unconditionally, which is why the hand-run deployment worked and the bundle path would not have. Both creates were also piped to Out-Null, hiding a genuine failure. Fix: discard both streams with `*> $null`, test `$LASTEXITCODE -eq 0` for existence, throw when a create fails, and repair the uninstall branch's inverted test. The stale pin that required `start= auto` (contradicting INSTALLER-BOOT-MODEL-001, and failing) now requires demand-start, refuses AUTO_START and requires install-boot-task.ps1. 5 new pins: the sc.exe stdout premise measured against the real binary, no truthiness test on sc.exe query in any spelling, every query followed by a LASTEXITCODE test, every create followed by throw-on-nonzero and never piped to Out-Null, and wfp_service.ps1's already-correct check preserved. tests/release: 135 passed.
commands: sc.exe query AegisNoSuchSvcXYZ (exit 1060, 122 bytes on stdout)
limitations: E2 + E1: the premise is measured and the fix is pinned structurally, but the installer has not been run elevated from this session, so service creation on a clean host is still the E5 gate.
The NSIS installer and the bundle script still differ in idempotency strategy (unconditional create vs query-then-create); unifying them is a separate decision.
Only the two services in install_aegis.ps1 were measured; other scripts that query kernel services were read but not exercised.

evidence.title: The boot loader reported success whenever it reached its last line
evidence.description: scripts/boot-sequence.ps1 ended with an unconditional `exit 0`, and its Last Result is what tools/host_preflight.py reads as `boot_task_last_result == 0`, so the check measured 'the loader reached its last line' rather than 'the stack came up': a boot where AegisWfp never loaded reported success. scripts/install-boot-task.ps1 decided that `sc.exe config AegisNids start= demand` succeeded by matching 'FAILED|denied' in the output; sc.exe localises its messages, so on a non-English host a real failure can match neither word and the script would log DEMAND_START over an AUTO_START service it never changed. Fix: the loader computes $ok from AegisWfp + AegisNids + AegisMinifilter, writes it into post-boot-probe.json, logs each service state when it is false and exits 1; the installer judges sc config by $LASTEXITCODE. 5 pins, two behavioural: the real script runs under a PowerShell function that shadows sc.exe, with PROGRAMDATA redirected to tmp_path, and is asserted to exit 0 with probe.ok true for the RUNNING stub and exit 1 with probe.ok false and 'NOT up' in the log for the STOPPED stub. tests/release/test_boot_model_scripts.py: 5 passed.
commands: powershell -NoProfile -File <harness with an sc.exe stub returning RUNNING|STOPPED>
limitations: E2, not E5: the exit code the scheduled task records on a real boot was not re-read from Task Scheduler; that needs the owner's reboot window.
The stub reproduces only the two fields the script parses (STATE : 4 RUNNING|STOPPED), not sc.exe behaviour.
install-boot-task.ps1 is pinned structurally only; its sc config path runs elevated against a real service.
boot_task_loader_installed stays FAIL on this host because the boot task points at admin-evidence, not C:\Program Files\AEGIS NIDS; that is the clean_host_e5 gate, unchanged by this patch.

evidence.title: The quarantine directory still ran: 28 scripts could rewrite tracked files
evidence.description: tools/legacy/ was described as quarantined but nothing enforced it. Its patchers rewrite tracked files if run (patch_graph_daemon.py -> scripts/aegis_graph.py; fix_console.py/fix_console2.py/update_console.py -> tools/aegisctl/commands/console.py; update_auth.py -> AUTHORITY_MAP.json, a truth artifact), and fix_console.py:95 held an unterminated f-string ("""" closing a triple-quoted block), so a repository-wide compile gate could not pass - the 2026-09-27 health audit recorded it as debt and it stayed. Fix: line 95 closes the f-string and the block, so the file parses; every one of the 28 tracked .py files now carries a quarantine header and a `raise SystemExit("QUARANTINED: <path> must not run...")` guard placed after any docstring and from __future__ import, leaving the historical bodies intact but unreachable, because the guard exits before any statement of the body. 61 pins: the census refuses a new unclassified file under the directory (and an allowlist entry naming a vanished file); per-file ast.parse refuses the fix_console.py:95 error class; per-file guard check refuses a file whose first statement is not the guard or a guard that does not name its own path; update_auth.py is executed for real and must exit non-zero without changing AUTHORITY_MAP.json's sha256; `compileall tools/legacy` must exit 0 (it exited 1 before); no product file in .py/.ps1/.zig/.go/.rs/.ts/.c/.nsi may name tools/legacy; and the orphan Rust crate must not be a Cargo workspace member or be named by a build file. Mutation control: deleting the guard from update_auth.py fails 2 pins, restoring returns 61 passed.
limitations: E2: no runtime behaviour changed, so there is nothing to verify at E5.
The guard is a runtime refusal, not a deletion; the bodies remain readable by design, and deleting the directory is an owner decision.
The orphan Rust crate is inert by absence (no workspace, no build file), which is not proof that nobody builds it by hand.
tools/legacy/Dashboard.py.before-unified-snapshot is allowlisted as data (no .py suffix, never executed) rather than guarded.

evidence.title: The zip bundle omitted the boot-model scripts its own installer executes
evidence.description: Two packaging paths install the product and they disagreed about the boot model. scripts/install_aegis.ps1 sets $bootSetup = Join-Path $InstallRoot 'scripts\install-boot-task.ps1' and throws when it is absent; scripts/install-boot-task.ps1 sets $boot = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'boot-sequence.ps1', throws when it is absent, and registers AegisBootSequence pointing at it. scripts/package_release.ps1 copied only install_aegis.ps1 and verify_release.ps1 into the bundle behind two Test-Path guards, so installing from the zip bundle on a host without a previous NSIS install copied the runtime, created AegisNids, then threw 'Boot-task installer missing'. Fix: one explicit $scriptPayload list (install_aegis, install-boot-task, boot-sequence, verify_release) that throws on a missing source instead of skipping it. 10 pins, all computed from the packaging sources rather than repeated in the test: what install_aegis.ps1 executes by path under $InstallRoot must be in the bundle payload; what installer.py executes via -File "$INSTDIR\scripts\..." must be in its File directives; the boot model must ship as a pair in both packagers; every shipped name must exist and be tracked; every file under scripts/ must have a classified suffix (54 .py compile via compileall, 61 .ps1 parse via the PowerShell AST, the .json loads, .bat/.cmd/.sh are NUL-free non-empty text); and install_aegis.ps1 must keep its fail-closed throw. Mutation control: deleting 'boot-sequence.ps1' from $scriptPayload fails test_the_boot_model_ships_as_a_pair_in_both_packagers, restoring returns 10 passed.
limitations: E2, not E4/E5: no bundle was built or installed here; 'the zip installs on a clean host' remains the clean_host_e5 gate.
The pins compare names, not bytes; the copies in the bundle are not hashed.
verify_release.ps1 is now mandatory for the bundle (it was conditional), a packaging behaviour change for a partial tree.
The entry proves every tracked script parses and every install-time script ships; it does not claim any e5_*/run_*_proof lab script was executed.

evidence.title: Two files under tools/ rewrote the tree when they were merely imported
evidence.description: AGENTS.md TEST HYGIENE rule 1 (tools modules importable with no socket, serve loop, stdout banner or sys.exit) was unchecked, and three files broke it. tools/update_health_cmd.py ran a patcher body at module scope: importing it read tools/aegisctl.py, 'replaced' cmd_health and wrote the file back, then printed Done - and it was stale, because getRuntimeHealth (the symbol its replacement imports) never appears in aegisctl.py, so it could only rewrite the tree for nothing; it moved to tools/legacy/ behind the LEGACY-INERT-001 quarantine guard. tools/create_manifest.py built the whole runtime manifest and wrote runtime_manifest.json (a truth artifact) at module scope; its body is now main() behind a __main__ guard, and two consecutive runs were verified to produce identical output apart from the date field. tools/probe_control_pipe.py dialled the live control pipe and printed JSON stages on import; the dial is now main(). New test imports every tracked tools/**.py module in a subprocess (package modules by dotted name so relative imports resolve as the CLI resolves them) and requires exit 0 with empty stdout and stderr; a second pin parses each file and refuses a module-scope write_text, open-for-write or json.dump so a future patcher fails even if the runtime probe is skipped; a census keeps the probed set equal to the tracked set. tools/legacy is excluded by construction (those files raise SystemExit at import by design). 82 pins, run with -W error::SyntaxWarning.
limitations: E2: no running component changed; this is import hygiene.
Each module is imported once, in-process, on this host; a side effect that needs a specific environment could pass here.
tools/legacy/ is exempt by construction - those files raise at import by design (LEGACY-INERT-001).
The static pin is syntactic: module-scope os.system/shutil.copy writes would escape it (the runtime probe would still catch a visible effect).
tools/etw_provider_probe.c and tools/run_zig_test_timeout.ps1 are not named by this entry: this slice did not compile or parse them.

evidence.title: Nothing checked that every src/ module was built, or that an unbuilt one said so
evidence.description: Five modules under src/ carry headers declaring their status (four QUARANTINED 'must never be wired into the daemon'; reliability.zig the G20-G33 specimen; federation.zig SUPERSEDED). tests/security/test_forbidden_edges.py already pinned that production modules do not import four of them, but nothing checked the other half: that every tracked .zig file is reachable from a build root at all, and that an unreachable one states its status in its own header. Measured: 293 tracked .zig files, 285 in the import closure of the eight .zig paths build.zig names (src/main.zig, all_tests.zig, compile_only_imports.zig, out_of_unit_tests.zig, fuzz_entry.zig, tests/federation/federation_tcp.zig, perf_bench_main.zig, integration_test_main.zig); 8 outside it. Two of the eight were silent: reliability.zig (611 lines) opened with a G20-G32 changelog and no word about being unwired despite carrying a second ReliabilityWatchdog, a stub SecurityCheck and drill-only canary/XDR types (the duplicate-authority shape AGENTS.md treats as stop-the-line), and federation.zig uses SUPERSEDED rather than QUARANTINED. Fix: reliability.zig now opens with SPECIMEN, NOT WIRED and names its live homes (watchdog/fault_injection/security_check/latency_histogram wired in daemon.zig) and states its inline tests do not run (comments only; zig build exits 0). New test computes the closure from the .zig paths build.zig names, asserts src/main.zig reaches no classified module, requires every tracked .zig to be reachable or in the census, fails when the census goes stale or when a classified file does not use its status word in its header, and floors the closure at 250 modules so a broken @import parser cannot pass silently. 30 passed together with test_forbidden_edges.py.
limitations: E2: reachability is a static @import walk, not a linker fact; @import arguments are string literals in Zig, which narrows but does not close the gap.
The closure begins where build.zig points; a root added by a script outside build.zig would be reported as an orphan (the intended failure).
This does not re-prove the forbidden-edge property; test_forbidden_edges.py owns it.
capture/npcap_test_live.zig is classified TOOL_ONLY rather than removed: giving it a target or deleting it is an owner decision.

evidence.title: The config validator crashed instead of reporting, and its report could crash too
evidence.description: Running the shipped validator against the shipped configs produced tracebacks, not diagnostics. `--config configs/aegis.conf` (a .conf file sitting next to the JSON configs) died with an uncaught JSONDecodeError and Python's exit code, and a wrong --schema path did the same via FileNotFoundError. Worse, `--config configs/policies.json` raised UnicodeEncodeError while PRINTING the failure report: the module's status literals were stored as mojibake (UTF-8 bytes decoded as cp1252 in the file's history) and a cp1252 console cannot encode them, so the report could crash where the config did not. Fix: main() wraps schema and config loading in try/except (OSError, ValueError) and returns exit 2 with 'ERROR: cannot read config <path> as JSON/TOML: ...' on stderr, names a non-object config, prints ASCII status lines (OK: / FAIL:), and prints --normalize output with ensure_ascii=True while file output keeps ensure_ascii=False. Verified on the real files: runtime.json -> 'OK: config valid' exit 0; aegis.conf -> exit 2 with a diagnostic; policies.json -> 4 'Missing required field' lines exit 1; missing schema -> exit 2. 31 pins: each of those behaviours runs the real CLI in a subprocess and forbids 'Traceback' in the combined output; a non-ASCII config filename must not turn a failure into UnicodeEncodeError; all 24 configs/**/*.json files parse; and no *.before-*/*.bak shadow copy may be named by the bundle payload. configs/Rules.json.before-reload-test is a genuinely stale snapshot (it lacks the rate_mode/rate_threshold/rate_window_ms fields and the tightened hosts regex of the live Rules.json) that 01-build-inventory.md already called an unclassified file that must not be packaged. Mutation control: removing the load_config try/except fails test_a_non_json_config_is_reported_not_traced_back; restoring returns 31 passed.
limitations: E2: jsonschema is not installed here, so validation ran through the module's required-key fallback; a schema-only violation was not exercised.
The stale rules shadow copy still exists; deleting a tracked file is a disposition decision, so the pins only keep it out of the package.
configs/aegis.conf is not validated by anything (the loader understands .json/.toml only); whether it is live configuration or documentation is unanswered.
Only configs/runtime.json was checked against the schema; the other 23 JSON files are pinned as parseable, not conformant (several are fixtures with a deliberate different shape).

evidence.title: The operator contract had no reader, and one of its claimants was two values short
evidence.description: contracts/operator_contract_v1.json declares the PolicyAction and PepDecision ordinal spaces and the rule that their BLOCK values must not be compared, but no code or test read it - git grep found it only in README, two design docs and generated maps. Comparing it to the code found drift: the contract and src/policy/pep_bindings.zig and the Rust DECISION_* constants all declare six PEP decisions (allow0 block1 rate_limit2 quarantine3 escalate4 drop5), while the duplicate enum in src/forensic/integration_contract.zig stopped at quarantine=3. Its inline Zig test checked exactly the four shared ordinals, so zig build test stayed green while the two Zig enums disagreed about the two values the assessment path returns (pep_bindings returns .escalate when the PEP is unavailable and guards on .drop). Fix: the forensic enum now declares all six with a comment naming pep_bindings.zig as the live authority and forbidding renumbering. shared/protocol/protocol_version.json had the same defect (no reader) for six constants that are duplicated in shared/wire/wire_codec.py. New test tests/contracts/test_operator_contract.py (8 pins): policy_action_ordinals equals PolicyAction in both src/contract/canonical_event.zig and src/forensic/policy_contract.zig; pep_decision_ordinals equals PepDecision in both Zig files and agrees with the Rust DECISION_* constants, and Rust still declares escalate/drop; PolicyAction.BLOCK != PepDecision.BLOCK, enforcing the file's own rule; the enforcement-receipt requirement list is non-empty and versioned; protocol_version.json equals WIRE_VERSION/WIRE_MAGIC/WIRE_HEADER_SIZE/WIRE_MAX_PAYLOAD/EVENT_MAGIC/EVENT_VERSION; and every un-fixtured contract file (contracts/operator_contract_v1.json, shared/protocol/protocol_version.json, shared/runtime/components.json) is named by some code or test in the working tree.

evidence.title: The PEP proof harness transposed quarantine and rate_limit in its action enum
evidence.description: Comparing every action-ordinal declaration found three numberings and one transposition. The canonical six-value space (allow0 alert1 block2 quarantine3 rate_limit4 log_only5) is declared identically in src/contract/canonical_event.zig, src/forensic/policy_contract.zig and src/policy/policy_engine.zig, but src/tests/proofs/pep_enforcement_proof.zig declared allow0 alert1 block2 rate_limit3 quarantine4 - the two restricted actions swapped - inside u8 fields of structs the proof compares, in the file whose output becomes evidence. Nothing executed wrongly because the proof compared tags, but a declared space that disagrees with the contract is inherited by any later ordinal cast, and src/policy/policy_contract.zig already has a test named 'quarantine and rate_limit are not interchangeable'. The second finding is that the FFI space was undocumented: src/policy/policy_ir.zig Action (pass0 log1 alert2 rate_limit3 block4 quarantine5 escalate6, mirrored exactly by ACTION_* in rust-src/lib.rs) is the requested_action ABI the Rust PEP receives per pep_bindings.zig, yet contracts/operator_contract_v1.json declared only two of the three spaces, so BLOCK reads as 2 in one document and 4 in the ABI with nothing saying why. Fix: the proof enum is renumbered to quarantine=3, rate_limit=4 with a comment naming the four modules sharing the space; the contract gains pep_request_action_ordinals plus a note that three spaces exist and none may be compared with another (convert, never cast); and tests/contracts/test_action_spaces.py pins all four canonical declarations equal to policy_action_ordinals, policy_ir.Action and Rust ACTION_* equal to pep_request_action_ordinals, the ordinal collision between the spaces (frozen 4=QUARANTINE equals FFI 4=BLOCK; frozen 2=BLOCK equals FFI 2=ALERT) so the note stays true, no .zig file casting an action into a canonical policy_action byte, and the existence of the intToEnum-based converter in policy_contract.zig. 16 passed together with test_operator_contract.py; zig build and zig build test exit 0. Mutation control: restoring the transposed proof enum fails test_canonical_action_space_is_identical_everywhere for that file; restoring returns 8 passed.
limitations: E2: the proof harness was not run against a live PEP; only its declared ordinal space was corrected.
The cast ban is syntactic and covers the two shapes present today; a cast through an intermediate variable would pass.
policy_ir.Action legitimately differs (it has pass and escalate); this documents it rather than unifying it, since unification is a wire change.
Rust ACTION_* is asserted equal to the contract, not directly to policy_ir.Action; the contract is the middle term.

evidence.title: An owner waiver is recorded as an exception, never as a passing soak gate
evidence.description: The owner decided to ship without waiting for the 24 h soak window. Both outputs keep 'NOT SHIPPABLE (waived by owner: soak_24h, unproven)' and the markdown lists what is not proven. 8 pins: a waiver never sets ok; a closed gate is not marked waived; malformed, unknown-gate, empty-not_proven and expired waivers are ignored; a future expiry is accepted; the verdict separates shippable from shippable_with_waiver; an unwaived open gate still blocks with the flag; a missing waivers file means no waivers. Observed: --release-check exit 1 with soak_24h WAIVED; --release-check --accept-waivers exit 0 with the same row.
limitations: The release is not 100 percent: five of six gates are proven, the sixth is waived by the owner and unproven.
Waivers are plain JSON in the repository, editable by anyone with commit access; they are governance, not cryptography.

evidence.title: L4 rule tagging is intermittent, loopback is not captured, and two gates of mine were unsound
evidence.description: Live measurement of whether an L4 rule tags a SYN scan, which ended with the first claim withdrawn. configs/Rules.json ships three L4 rules with real rate configuration (R9006 distinct_dst_ports 20/10000 ms, R9002 count 50/1000 ms, R9007 per-packet FLAGS) and src/pipeline/event_processor.zig:307 evaluates them for ev.source == .capture_npcap, which canonical Go-Nose frames map to via event_queue.legacySourceFor. Run 1, three trials: a 150-port loopback SYN scan produced no rule-tagged record, and across 1000 retained records none carried a non-zero rule_id. A later full-suite run XPASSed twice, but the test counted any tagged record; restricted to npcap_sensor records, three scan rounds produced zero tagged records and the test returned to xfail, so the XPASSes were almost certainly file/registry detections (the daemon does tag that telemetry) rather than the scan. evidence.title: The 24 h soak window fails on shed_overload 15163 vs budget 4000, caused by operator gates running inside it
evidence.description: At 16.95 h the soak tool returned verdict FAIL with one problem: shed_overload grew by 15163 inside the window (baseline 0) exceeding the policy-shed budget 4000. evidence.title: The runtime lifecycle is reconciled on a timer, with hysteresis, instead of sampled once at startup
evidence.description: DEFECT-READY-001: src/daemon.zig sampled bridge_init.allActive() once after init and moved the lifecycle to degraded if any bridge was not yet attested, and nothing re-evaluated it. recomputeHealth() mapped failed->degraded and degraded->recovering but had no timer and no caller for recovering->running, so status said DEGRADED for the life of the process while health, derived from live facts, said RUNNING. The patch moves the rule into RuntimeState.reconcileLifecycle(now_ms, facts): the facts are the same four booleans the health contract publishes (pipeline_ready, pipeline_failed, bridge_ready, data_loss_observed) plus subsystem health; any disagreeing fact demotes immediately (running or recovering -> degraded) because a real failure must not be averaged away; promotion needs PROMOTION_SAMPLES=3 consecutive clear samples at least PROMOTION_MIN_INTERVAL_MS=5000 apart, so a fast poll cannot accumulate evidence, and the streak resets after each step so RECOVERING -> RUNNING pays its own three samples. daemon.lifecycleLoop supplies the facts every five seconds and is joined by the supervisor on shutdown; data_loss_observed is new loss since the previous sample, so a cumulative counter cannot pin the runtime degraded forever and recent loss is not averaged away. Four tests in state_machine.zig pin the promote path, streak reset on one bad sample, the loss guard, the fast-poll guard and immediate demotion. zig build test exits 0.
limitations: E2 only: the live host still runs the previously installed build, so the promotion has not been observed on a process yet.

evidence.title: Live HTTP protocol anomalies 10004/10001/10003 from a bridged Kali on the shipped Wi-Fi sensor path
evidence.description: Closes the IDS-L7-003 blocker with two live RB-022 windows on the path the release ships. The canonical Go Nose attaches up to 1,024 raw frame bytes as a v3 payload and event_queue.legacySourceFor maps npcap_sensor to capture_npcap, so the anomaly lane runs without a lab pin or a restart. A Kali 2025.2 VM bridged to the LAN (192.168.1.207) sent malformed HTTP to this host (192.168.1.39) python http.server on 8080. Window wifi-bridged-l7-20261117 (150 s) attributed 2 rows to rule 10004 with dropped/shed/quota_shed deltas 0. Window wifi-bridged-l7-kinds-20261117 (120 s) attributed 6 rows (10004 x2, 10001 x2, 10003 x2) with the same zero loss deltas; a well-formed control produced none. Every row is enforcement_status observed, host_effect_confirmed false, policy pass, with a v1 IDS receipt hash and sequence. Measured triggers: no Host header (10004), a 20-byte alphabetic method (10001), and a version that does not start with HTTP/ (10003); the old runbook shapes BOGUS and HTTP/9.9 do not trip their checks. Each request produced two rows because this Killer Wi-Fi/Npcap path delivers every frame twice (single-handle dumpcap: identical ip.id and TCP seq ~7 us apart, one Ethernet interface; a VMnet1 ARP control shows no duplication), recorded as CAPTURE-DUP-WIFI-001. evidence.title: One automaton per rule layer: kernel rules no longer fire on network bytes
evidence.description: reloadRules() used to load every non-L4 rule into one automaton and processEvent() ran it over every source's payload, so HTTP/TLS bytes containing IEX were tagged R2003 (KERNEL_PROCESS) and FIM paths could be tagged with network rules. The loader now maps each rule's layer to its own automaton (network, kernel_file, kernel_process, l2_pipe), builds the non-network automata while the rules JSON is still alive, and swaps all four under g_ac_mutex; the processor picks one by the event source and counts sources that have no layer instead of matching them against another layer's catalog. g_active_ac stays the network automaton and loadRulesInto() is untouched, so existing readers and single-automaton tests keep working, and a rule without a layer field still loads as network rather than being dropped. Pins: ruleLayer() mapping; a network automaton holding R9059 does not match IEX while a kernel_process automaton does and the network one still matches its own rule; ruleLayerIndexForSource() maps npcap/wfp to 0, fim/registry to 1, etw to 2, pipe_monitor to 3 and host_net/detection_brain/system to null. zig build and zig build test exit 0.
limitations: E2 only: no live attribution has been observed on wire bytes yet; the E5 check needs an HTTP listener on VMnet1 plus payloads from Kali and forensics attribution by source and rule.
The per-layer distribution inside reloadRules() is not unit-pinned; the pins cover the layer mapping and the automata, and the distribution rests on build plus the pending live check.
A layer automaton that fails to build falls back to the network automaton (old over-matching), logged, rather than matching nothing.
A source change restarts the soak clock, so the 24 h window has to start after the rebuilt binary is installed.

evidence.title: Wire payloads carry only L7 rule ids and kernel rules only fire on host sources, on the installed build
evidence.description: The layered split was first installed and the check FAILED on the live host: a UDP payload carrying IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient) sent over VMnet1 was tagged R2003 (KERNEL_PROCESS) and ambient 1271-byte traffic was tagged R3003 (L2_PIPE, pattern 'anonymous'), because the startup path built a single automaton and the pipeline fell back to it, and because the first version of the split added every non-L4 rule to the network automaton as well as to its layer. Both were fixed: daemon startup now runs the layered reload (log line 'layered rules at startup: loaded 23 (network=5 kernel_file=5 kernel_process=5 l2_pipe=5)'), and the network automaton holds only network rules. The installed binary sha256 abf1a4ae469c2b017bf387ecca880e248d4fcae6a31e5b4ed5596f5ef08f938a equals zig-out/bin/aegis_nids.exe. Measured on the running service: three UDP frames carrying '<script>alert(1)</script>' produced exactly R9059 (hash 4009890390, L7) and three carrying '../../etc/passwd' produced exactly R0088 (hash 4254503461, L7), each also seen from the VM side (192.168.126.10), while the same frames were NOT tagged with R1001/R1002/R1003/R2001-R2005/R3001-R3003. The stimulus was host-originated UDP over VMnet1, not an HTTP request from the Kali guest: the guest could not be driven for exec (vmrun runProgramInGuest returns 'A file was not found'), so the wire bytes came from the host side of the same captured interface.

evidence.title: The forensic ring is searchable by payload text (payload_contains), proven live with a negative control
evidence.description: The ring had no way to answer the operator's real question (which record carries this text?). payload_prefix compares stored bytes from byte 0, and on capture rows byte 0 is the L2 header, so a readable string can never match -- an operator typing text got records_matched 0 with no way to tell 'not retained' from 'no match'. This slice adds payload_contains to forensics.list: a substring search over exactly the payload span (payload_start..payload_end, never the header, never past payload_len). Measured on the installed build f57f232089c6c652 (same sha256 as zig-out/bin/aegis_nids.exe, service RUNNING): four UDP frames carrying 'GET /contains-canary?q=<script>alert(1)</script>' from 192.168.126.1 to 192.168.126.10:9999 produced 'forensic search --field payload_contains --value contains-canary' = 8 matched and '--field rule --value R9059' = 8 matched (four frames, both directions), while the negative control '--value zzz-not-present-zzz' = 0. Rule search was NOT broken: the earlier 0 result was ring retention (18.7 M records appended, bounded slots), which this entry corrects rather than repeats.
limitations: The scan covers the retained ring window only; a 0 can still mean 'aged out' rather than 'never seen', and the response does not yet say which sequence range was scanned.
The frames came from the host side of VMnet1 (the Kali guest cannot be driven for exec on this host), so the source is host-originated traffic on the captured interface.

evidence.title: Option B measured: batching cannot amortise a per-record serial hash over the whole slot
evidence.description: Measured the mandatory per-record pass of the forensic append with the ring's own primitives (crc32_slicing.Crc32.hash and std.crypto.hash.sha2.Sha256), 20,000 iterations at -OReleaseSafe on the host the product runs on: memset over 4 KiB 50 ns, SHA-256 over the 4,092-byte span the chain covers 2,387 ns, CRC32 slicing-by-8 over the same span 1,792 ns -- 4.2 us total, against a live stage=forensic_append p50 of 16.4 us. A 200-byte header+payload span hashes in 176 ns. So option B (batched append) can amortise only the memset and the lock (~50 ns of 4,200 ns, ~1%) because the hash chain is per-record and serial and covers the whole slot by contract; the ~14x win needs the hashed span narrowed, which is an integrity-contract change and is recorded as such in docs/adr/0014-q-loss-ingress-isolation.md rather than implemented silently.
limitations: This is a measurement of the primitives, not of a storm: it says what B can save, not what the ceiling becomes.
The benchmark file was a throwaway and has been deleted; the numbers live in the ADR.

known_gaps.description: Operator report: a blank 'Administrator: ...python.exe' console kept popping while the system ran. known_gaps.title: L4 rules are per-packet predicates, not rate/window flood or scan detectors
known_gaps.description: R9006 fired on any exact SYN (normal handshakes included); R9002 on any ICMP echo/reply; R9007 on exact FIN+PSH+URG. No rate, window, or scan-pattern state existed at discovery. The rule names (TCP SYN Stealth Scan, ICMP Flood) implied rate semantics that were not implemented. The 2026-10-20 lab is explicit about this: a 100-port nmap scan produced 200 matching packets and 300 hping3 ICMP packets produced 300 rows -- per-packet matches, not flood/scan verdicts.
required_evidence: rate/window state and threshold tests for SYN/ICMP, or an explicit rename/reclassification to per-packet predicates
negative control showing normal handshakes/pings below a threshold do not fire
known_gaps.resolution: Implemented opt-in L4 rate/window semantics in src/pipeline/l4_matcher.zig, config-driven by configs/Rules.json. R9002: count >=50 ICMP packets per source per 1000 ms. R9006: >=20 distinct destination ports per source per 10000 ms. Both emit once per source/window; R9007 remains exact FIN|PSH|URG per-packet. The tracker keys rule + full source address + IPv4/IPv6 identity, is a fixed 256-entry table, and resets on rules reload. Zig tests cover the 49th-vs-50th ICMP boundary, 19-vs-20 distinct-port boundary, duplicate-port suppression, once-per-window emission/re-arm, source and address-family separation, reset, and the stateless R9007 path; negative controls prove a normal single handshake and sub-threshold pings do not fire. Config pins are in tests/security/test_l4_rate_config.py. This closes the code-semantics gap at E2; the installed 04F9... artifact (2026-10-20) later proved R9002 live at E5, while R9006/R9007 live proof is now recorded on the canonical Nose path and in the isolated lab.

known_gaps.title: Native FIM ReadDirectoryChangesW watcher discards an overflown 64 KiB batch without a counter
known_gaps.description: During the FIM-half QLOSS storm (QLOSS-FIMSTORM-003-E5-20261118) the native watcher delivered 1,167 notifications for 20,004 creates + 20,004 deletes. A 100-file control batch on the same daemon yields exactly one native notification per file operation, so ~40,008 were expected; 38,841 (97.1%) went missing while batch_overflow stayed 0 and every loss counter stayed 0. src/windows/fim_native.c:112-132 treats a zero-byte completion as 'no data' (GetOverlappedResult succeeds with bytes_returned == 0 when the directory buffer overflows) and never reads ERROR_NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR, so the whole batch is dropped silently. The minifilter lane observed the same operations (40,353 records), which is why the pipeline still held in this run.
tests: E5: native_poll +1,167 of ~40,008 expected under the 20k burst; batch_overflow 0; no fim overflow counter exists
E5 control: 100 files -> native_poll +100 on create and +100 on delete, so the expected yield is one record per operation
known_gaps.finding: This is silent event loss in a telemetry component, which AGENTS.md lists as a stop-the-line condition. It did not become pipeline loss here because the minifilter lane covered the same operations, so the finding is scoped to the native watcher being an untrustworthy fallback rather than to host coverage in this window. No fix was written in the measurement window.
required_evidence: Count zero-byte/ERROR_NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR completions in fim_native.c and expose the total in queue.stats as a FIM-native overflow counter (never a silent continue).
E5 re-run of the same 20k storm: delivered native records plus the new overflow counter account for the full expected count.
Decide whether the native watcher remains a fallback lane for production System32/SysWOW64 or is retired in favour of the minifilter under burst.
known_gaps.tracking: Local stop-the-line record (AGENTS.md: silent event loss); no GitHub issue filed
known_gaps.resolution: The helper now counts both overflow completions (ERROR_NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR and the zero-byte success) per session, the Zig watcher publishes the delta and queue.stats exposes fim_probe.native_overflow. E5 re-run: control batch 0 overflows, 20k storm 7 discarded batches with every pipeline loss counter at 0 and the minifilter covering 40,320 records; R1002 still fires. The lane stays as a counted fallback; record-level loss inside a discarded batch is unrecoverable by API design and is recorded as a limitation.
known_gaps.next_step: If the native lane is ever promoted back to primary, bound or re-tune the 500 ms poll cadence in its own change and soak; the counter already makes the loss visible in the meantime.

known_gaps.title: The Aho-Corasick matcher applies KERNEL_PROCESS payload rules to network bytes, so TLS traffic raises R2003
known_gaps.detail: R2003 (PowerShell Cradle Download, layer KERNEL_PROCESS, pattern IEX|DownloadString|DownloadFile|PS_CRADLE|Net.WebClient) matched 366 wire events: 291 with src_port 443, 324 at the 1024-byte Nose attachment cap, remote IPv6/IPv4 sources, dst_port absent. src/pipeline/event_processor.zig:280 runs the AC matcher over qe.payload for every source except capture_host_net and never consults the rule's layer, so a three-byte token inside an encrypted TLS record becomes a PowerShell-cradle detection. Every row is enforcement_status observed with host_effect_confirmed false (prevention gate closed), so this is alert quality, not host authority. Found while establishing the negative control for DETECT-L4-001: the victim host's own outbound TLS session produced an attributed row that had nothing to do with the stimulus.
known_gaps.blocked_by: the fix is a src/ edit (event_processor.zig AC rule selection by layer/source); the release runtime 7c604d5 is signed, installed and soaked, so a source change needs a new build, signature, install and window (v1.1), not a patch to this release

known_gaps.closed_note: Layered automata are in the installed build and the live attribution is correct: wire payloads carry only L7 ids (R9059, R0088) and never a kernel id, while R1001/R1002/R1003 still fire on host sources. Both are fixed in the installed binary abf1a4ae. Re-measured 2026-11-17 21:26 with one frame carrying both the L7 and the kernel-process pattern: only R9059 (L7) fired, never R2003 (RULE-LAYER-SCOPE-001-E5-20261117c).
