known_gaps.found_by: single-handle dumpcap capture taken while closing IDS-L7-003
known_gaps.title: The Wi-Fi capture path delivers every frame twice, doubling detections and anomaly rows
known_gaps.detail: On the Killer Wi-Fi 6 AX1650i (NPF_{5FD31C6E-DE48-44CB-838E-14667A04DA4B}) Npcap delivers every frame twice to a capture handle: SYN, payload and FIN each appear in a pair with identical ip.id, TCP sequence and bytes, about 7 us apart, in a file with one Ethernet interface block. AEGIS therefore emits two events per wire frame, so protocol_anomaly and signature_match counts and nose_frames_read/submitted are about 2x the wire count. Attribution and verdicts stay correct; this is evidence/throughput inflation on one adapter, not a double enqueue. Excluded as the cause: the product path (nose/capture.go:154-183 emits one event per ReadPacketData; nose_pipe_reader.zig:381-430 pushes one frame per pipe frame; duplicate and non-monotonic id counters are 0), VMware (host-sourced traffic duplicates too), and generic Npcap (a VMnet1 ARP control captured 3 pings as 3 frames).
known_gaps.impact: Halve counts on this adapter when reading detections, anomaly rows or frame rates. No capture_npcap drops were observed in the measured windows; the doubled work has not caused loss.
known_gaps.next_step: host configuration first (no source change): test Dot11Support=0 or an Npcap reinstall without raw 802.11 and re-measure duplication; if it persists, add a bounded, counted dedup keyed by (ip.id, tcp.seq, payload hash) that cannot drop a real retransmission. The lab path uses Kali on VMnet1, which does not duplicate; the Wi-Fi doubling only affects the production nose path. Do not patch this into the signed T20 runtime.
known_gaps.observed_in: admin-evidence/wifi-dup-20261117/wifi-dup-45007.tshark.txt and vmnet1-control-arp.tshark.txt (local-only); anomaly windows in admin-evidence/lab-wifi-bridged-l7-20261117 and lab-wifi-bridged-l7-kinds-20261117
known_gaps.status_basis: closed 2026-11-17 at E5 by CAPTURE-DUP-BYTE-LEVEL-E5-20261117: a raw-byte probe (equal length + equal sha256 within 2 ms) finds 5/14 duplicated host_tx frames in the 02:39 capture and 0 in 29,060 frames across 19 captures taken later the same day, with Dot11Support 0 and 1, at up to 1,126 fps, and with the Go Nose handle attached
known_gaps.closed_note: The counter this gap was opened with keyed on (src, dst, ip.id, tcp.seq|udp.length, len) and therefore counted TCP Dup ACKs, which repeat Seq/Ack with Len=0 and no payload; tshark labels those pairs '[TCP Dup ACK]' and they carry no IPv4 addresses. Byte-identical delivery is the only signature a capture-path duplicate can produce, and that signature is absent from every capture taken after the earlier Wi-Fi association ended at 03:35:05 (WLAN event 11004); the current association started at 14:31:01. The product path is also excluded on its own evidence: nose emitted one canonical event per captured frame (26300/26300/0 dropped) and VMnet1 never duplicated. The 02:39 observation is preserved, not explained.
known_gaps.remaining: None actionable now. Root cause of the 02:39 event is unidentified and not claimed. The byte-level probe (g3_dup_bytes.py) is the reopen instrument: a nonzero identical-byte pair count on the Wi-Fi adapter in a normal (no lab artifact) state reopens this gap with the capture and its hash.
known_gaps.not_run: high-rate arm at Dot11Support=0 (UAC dismissed twice), any second SSID/association, and a root-cause trace of the 02:39 doubling

known_gaps.found_by: tagging v2.0.0 and comparing the signed SHA256SUMS digest with the git blob
known_gaps.title: The signed SHA256SUMS digest is checkout-EOL dependent, so a fresh clone cannot re-derive it
known_gaps.detail: release/T20-final/9ebee9b/signatures.json signs digest 9F87BF36D28149F5FEF22B997DC6928C8846A69D5468D1BD3D5E91367A6931BC, which is the sha256 of the CRLF file on disk. The git blob for the same path stores LF and hashes to 668C26B10FA24BBC0EFC4910B559A3225A8A21B1B95CF6C0F38F935C1063DFA2; replacing LF with CRLF in the blob reproduces the signed digest exactly, so the content is identical and only line endings differ. The release tree has not changed since commit 1a0e77f added it (git diff 1a0e77f..HEAD over release/T20-final/9ebee9b is empty), and the working tree copy verifies against the signature. Nothing that ships is affected; what is limited is third-party re-derivation of the signed digest from a clean checkout where core.autocrlf is false.
known_gaps.impact: A verifier on a LF checkout computes 668C26B1... and may report a signature mismatch even though the shipped file is the signed one. release_engineering.py --verify passes on this host because the working tree is CRLF.
known_gaps.next_step: v1.1: make the release verifier hash a normalised form (or publish the digest over the normalised bytes), state CRLF as a hard checkout requirement in KNOWN_LIMITATIONS, and add a test that a fresh checkout reproduces the signed digest. Do not change the signed artifact itself.
known_gaps.closed_note: tools/verify_release_digest.py accepts the stored CRLF digest or the LF->CRLF normalised digest, says which form matched, and fails on tampered content; tests/release/test_release_digest_eol.py pins the shipped tree, an LF checkout, a tampered line, a missing signature and the exit code. The signed SHA256SUMS and signatures.json are unchanged.
known_gaps.remaining: None for verification. Publishing the digest over a normalised form or forcing CRLF at checkout would be a v1.1 packaging change, not an open evidence gap.

known_gaps.title: forensic search could not answer by payload text (payload_prefix can never match capture rows)
known_gaps.description: Measured 2026-11-18 on the installed build: 'aegisctl forensic search --field rule --value R9059' and '--field payload_prefix --value GET /scan' both return records_matched 0, records_returned 0, truncated false, on a ring of 18.7 M records, while 'aegisctl events tail --count 20 --src-ip 192.168.126.1 --json' shows R9059 rows produced minutes earlier from the same stimulus. Candidates: the client-side rule hashing in the search path differs from hashRuleId; the scan window does not cover the records; or payload_prefix is compared against the wrong byte span. It matters because searching the ring is the operator's only way back from a record to its bytes, and the 2026-11-17 note that payload-prefix returns 0 on this build is an unexplained defect rather than a usage quirk (the correct invocation is --field payload_prefix --value ...; --json is not accepted there).
known_gaps.next_step: Compare the search path's rule hashing with the runtime hashRuleId, confirm which records the scan walks, and pin the result; then re-measure both fields with a stimulus whose rule id is known.
known_gaps.closed_note: payload_contains is implemented in forensics.list and exposed by the CLI; on the installed build the filter matched 8/8 records for a canary string while a nonsense value matched 0, and rule search matched the same 8. The 0 result that opened this gap was ring retention, not a broken rule filter -- recorded here because the original claim was wrong.
known_gaps.remaining: A 0 can still mean 'aged out of the retained window'; the response does not yet report the scanned sequence range, so that ambiguity is documented, not removed.

known_gaps.title: Command-line visibility is unavailable from both process lanes; R2003 is an accepted limitation
known_gaps.description: Resolved half (now E2; originally recorded E5, PROC-LAYER-001-E5-20261118): the layer follows the event kind, so process-create rows reach the kernel_process automaton and R2004 fires on a real certutil launch. The remaining question was answered in the 2026-11-18 operator-attested window (now E2 in this index): the ETW helper was rebuilt with WINEVENT_KEYWORD_PROCESS and the service restarted after install, process_start advanced with zero drops, and a marker launch produced a 306-byte ETW process row without the marker. Get-WinEvent shows every ProcessStart template (v0..v4) has ImageName and no CommandLine field, so no keyword mask can add it. The minifilter lane pushes only the image path (61 bytes) by construction. R2003 cannot match a host process row; R2001/R2002/R2005 still match image names and R2004 was proven live earlier. S1 (493648f) later added a read-only producer so the source half of FN-1 is no longer an accepted limitation; host proof is still pending.
known_gaps.next_step: S1 (493648f, E2 2026-11-25) added a read-only ProcessStart command-line producer via NtQueryInformationProcess and proved TLV->R2003 at E2. Host E5 re-measurement (long-lived IEX cradle -> one R2003 row, benign/wire-only -> zero) remains owner action; see S1-R2003-CMDLINE-PRODUCER-20261125.md.

known_gaps.title: Full-suite zig build test is nondeterministic: the test process dies at xdr prune in some runs, and all XDR tests pass alone
known_gaps.description: Three consecutive full-suite runs on 2026-11-18 ended with "while executing test 'xdr.xdr_engine.test.XdrEngine prune', the following test command failed" (2103/2114 passed, 1 failed, 10 skipped). Between those runs and the next one the only changes were records and tooling: no XDR or test-runner source was touched. A fourth full-suite run exited 0, and `zig test ... --test-filter XdrEngine` passes 11/11 in isolation, as does the adapter suite in isolation. The wording is the build runner reporting that the test *process* died while that test was executing, not an assertion failure, so either the test binary itself is intermittently corrupting memory or a thread leaked by an earlier test faults there. Attribution to XdrEngine is therefore provisional.
known_gaps.next_step: No source change is justified. If the failure recurs, reopen with the full runner log, the build summary, host memory pressure and the exact source SHA; do not count a cached-green run.

known_gaps_status_note: status is one of OPEN, CLOSED, CLOSED_AT_RECORDED_HEAD or UNRECORDED. CLOSED_AT_RECORDED_HEAD means the entry's own result field recorded a pass/closure at the head_sha it names (status_basis repeats it) and nobody has re-verified it at the current HEAD; it is a historical record, not a current guarantee. UNRECORDED means the entry carries no recorded result and has not been assessed. Neither field is ever promoted to CLOSED by this index alone. CLOSED_AT_RECORDED_HEAD additionally requires a 7-40 hex head_sha and a non-empty result field; entries lacking either are UNRECORDED (P3-EVIDENCE-HONESTY).
